basics.name: Xingtian (James) Si
basics.summary: M.A. Economics student at the University of Chicago. Researcher in causal inference and causal machine learning, with a focus on consumer behavior, targeting, and policy evaluation.

work.organization: University of California, San Diego (RA for Prof. Sally Sadoff)
work.position: Research Assistant — Correspondence Audit Studies on Labor Market Discrimination
highlights: Processed participant-level data from 10,000+ respondents (44,000+ observations) across 8 name-perception studies using Python.
Constructed a structured 53-sheet database tracing the provenance of 600+ fictitious names across 22 correspondence audit studies.

work.position: Independent Research — When Click-to-Cancel Creates Complexity: A Theory of Subscription Regulation
highlights: Developed a partial-equilibrium model of joint cancellation-friction and retention-menu complexity choice; proved a waterbed effect under California's AB 2863.
Derived the welfare condition under which click-to-cancel regulation benefits consumers.

work.position: Undergraduate Dissertation — Causal Machine Learning and Counterfactual Inference in Consumer Behavior
highlights: Applied causal random forests, TMLE, and BART in R and Python to estimate average and heterogeneous treatment effects of coupon and advertising interventions.
Designed a personalized coupon allocation framework with R Shiny dashboards under budget constraints.

work.organization: Columbia University (RA for Dr. Jiaxi Yang)
work.position: Research Assistant — HTE of Early Childhood Interventions on Fifth-Grade Math Achievement
highlights: Extracted and merged longitudinal ECLS-K:2011 data (n ≈ 18,000) with sample weights and multiple imputation (MICE).
Trained causal random forests (R grf), identifying an approximately 0.15 SD improvement among high-risk children.

work.organization: University of Nottingham (RA for Prof. Abigail Barr)
work.position: Research Assistant — Board Gender Diversity and Firm Performance in the UK
highlights: Estimated linear and nonlinear panel models on 840 firm-year observations (2008–2016) using Stata.
Identified an inverted-U relationship between female director share and Tobin's Q, moderated by firm size; published in Entrepreneurship and Innovation.
